caseResults.title: Prototype Pollution in minimist argument parsing
caseResults.name: minimist

actualFindings.title: Prototype pollution still reachable via constructor.prototype path
actualFindings.recommendation: Also block 'constructor' and 'prototype' when walking intermediate keys, for example `if (key === '__proto__' || key === 'constructor' || key === 'prototype') return;`. Better still, only traverse own properties (`Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(o, key)`) or create containers with `Object.create(null)`. Apply the same guard to the final key assigned after the loop.

goldenFindings.rationale: Direct traversal of __proto__ key allows remote attackers to pollute Object.prototype

findings.title: Guard covers only intermediate keys, not the final assigned key
findings.recommendation: The check sits inside the loop that runs to `keys.length - 1`, so the last key is never validated. Apply the blocklist to the final key as well as the intermediate ones, or use a shared `isUnsafeKey` helper. Any code that assigns `o[lastKey]` outside this loop needs the same defense.

findings.title: Prototype pollution guard permits constructor.prototype traversal
findings.recommendation: Reject '__proto__', 'constructor', and 'prototype' in every path segment, including the final key, before traversal or assignment. The supplied loop allows constructor.prototype.polluted to reach Object.prototype; add a regression test for this bypass.

caseResults.title: Prototype Pollution in ini file section decoding
caseResults.name: ini

actualFindings.title: Incomplete Prototype Pollution Protection via Section Name
actualFindings.recommendation: Strictly block 'constructor' and 'prototype' in addition to '__proto__', or validate section names against an allowlist and ensure objects are initialized with Object.create(null) or guarded against prototype traversal.

goldenFindings.rationale: Unsanitized section key allows __proto__ property injection during INI decoding

findings.title: Incomplete Prototype Pollution Protection via Section Name
findings.recommendation: Strictly block 'constructor' and 'prototype' in addition to '__proto__', or validate section names against an allowlist and ensure objects are initialized with Object.create(null) or guarded against prototype traversal.

findings.title: Incomplete prototype pollution guard: only '__proto__' is blocked, 'constructor' and inherited Object.prototype keys are not
findings.recommendation: Don't use a single-string denylist. Create the output and section containers with Object.create(null), or look sections up with Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(out, section) instead of `out[section] || {}`. If a denylist is kept, it must cover '__proto__', 'constructor' and 'prototype', and the same check must also be applied to key names assigned onto p. Add tests for `[constructor]`, `[prototype]`, `[toString]` and `[hasOwnProperty]` sections.

findings.title: Section lookup `out[section] || {}` still reads inherited properties
findings.recommendation: An untrusted section header such as `[constructor]` resolves `out['constructor']` to the inherited global Object function, which is truthy. `p` then points at that shared object, so later key assignments write onto a global object. Use an own-property check or a null-prototype container for `out` and for every section object.

findings.title: Section guard still permits inherited constructor objects
findings.recommendation: Reject '__proto__', 'constructor', and 'prototype' section names. Use null-prototype dictionaries and own-property checks when selecting section objects so inherited properties cannot become assignment targets.

caseResults.title: Prototype Pollution in JSON-Patch constructor/prototype path
caseResults.name: fast-json-patch

actualFindings.title: The prototype guard skips the final path segment, so '__proto__' can still be assigned as a leaf key
actualFindings.recommendation: Run the banned-key check on every segment, including keys[keys.length - 1], and do it before the loop and before any read or write. Better still, reject '__proto__', 'constructor' and 'prototype' outright in any position. Also use Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(obj, key) instead of obj[key] === undefined, and create intermediate containers with Object.create(null) or only write to own properties. The loop runs to keys.length - 1, so a path such as '/a/__proto__' with an object value reaches the final assignment (outside this diff) with key '__proto__'. That assignment calls the __proto__ setter and replaces the prototype of the target object with attacker-controlled data. For path '/__proto__' the loop does not run at all, so the document's own prototype can be swapped.

goldenFindings.rationale: Unvalidated constructor/prototype path components allow prototype attribute mutation

findings.title: The prototype guard skips the final path segment, so '__proto__' can still be assigned as a leaf key
findings.recommendation: Run the banned-key check on every segment, including keys[keys.length - 1], and do it before the loop and before any read or write. Better still, reject '__proto__', 'constructor' and 'prototype' outright in any position. Also use Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(obj, key) instead of obj[key] === undefined, and create intermediate containers with Object.create(null) or only write to own properties. The loop runs to keys.length - 1, so a path such as '/a/__proto__' with an object value reaches the final assignment (outside this diff) with key '__proto__'. That assignment calls the __proto__ setter and replaces the prototype of the target object with attacker-controlled data. For path '/__proto__' the loop does not run at all, so the document's own prototype can be swapped.

findings.title: A bare 'constructor' segment is not blocked, so global constructors can be written to (only the 'constructor' → 'prototype' pair is rejected)
findings.recommendation: Block 'constructor' unconditionally as a path segment, not only when 'prototype' follows it. Alternatively, traverse only own properties, so that obj['constructor'] cannot resolve to the inherited Object or Function constructor. A path such as '/constructor/x' resolves obj.constructor to the global Object function and then writes Object.x. A path such as '/constructor/constructor/x' writes Function.x. Both tamper with shared global state even though Object.prototype itself is protected. The check is also order-sensitive. It depends on keys[i - 1] being exactly 'constructor' and on 'prototype' appearing as an intermediate key. It is a blocklist and is easy to bypass if the path is normalized or decoded differently upstream, for example JSON Pointer '~' escapes or percent-encoding.

findings.title: Prototype guard skips the final path segment
findings.recommendation: Validate every decoded path segment before traversal or leaf mutation. The loop excludes the final segment, leaving paths such as /__proto__ and /constructor/prototype unchecked at their final key. Reject __proto__, constructor, and prototype consistently, including single-segment paths.

caseResults.title: ReDoS via greedy whitespace regex in semver
caseResults.name: semver

actualFindings.title: cleanVersion 對含多個前後空白的輸入改為回傳 null(行為回歸)
actualFindings.recommendation: 原 regex `^\s*...\s*$` 的 `\s*` 與相鄰的 `[0-9]+` 字元集互不重疊,且以 `^` 錨定,匹配時間為線性,並非 ReDoS。把 `\s*` 改成 `\s{0,1}` 並沒有消除實際風險,卻讓 `"  1.2.3"`、`"1.2.3  "` 這類輸入從通過變成 null。請還原為 `re[0]`;若要防禦過長輸入,改在比對前加輸入長度上限(例如 `str.length <= 256`),並補上多個空白輸入的回歸測試。

actualFindings.title: Whitespace restriction rejects previously accepted versions
actualFindings.recommendation: Preserve arbitrary surrounding whitespace by trimming the input before matching an anchored version regex. Verify that inputs such as " 1.2.3 " and "  1.2.3  " both return "1.2.3". The original anchored regex has no nested or overlapping quantifiers that establish a ReDoS vulnerability.

goldenFindings.rationale: Greedy whitespace quantifier in version parsing regex causes ReDoS

actualFindings.title: Code injection via outputFunctionName in template compilation
actualFindings.recommendation: Validate that opts.outputFunctionName is a primitive string, reject JavaScript reserved words, and ensure non-string objects with mutable toString coercion cannot bypass validation before dynamic statement interpolation into the function body.

goldenFindings.rationale: Unvalidated outputFunctionName identifier allows arbitrary statement interpolation and RCE
